sections.h2: Greenbrier Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 170 residential sales closed in Greenbrier (Chesapeake, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $275,000, below the citywide median of $420,000, and homes took a median of 18 days to sell, about the same pace as the citywide median of 18 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of Greenbrier sales closed between $227,750 and $365,000, or about $225 per square foot against $219 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($289,950, 88 sales) was about 12% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($260,000, 82 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

Recent Greenbrier sales were in ZIP code 23320.

12% of Greenbrier sales had four or more bedrooms, against 53% citywide. 32% of sales here were detached homes, versus 76% citywide. The median Greenbrier home is about 1,256 square feet, smaller than the 1,970 square foot citywide median.

sections.h2: When Greenbrier Homes Sell and How Far Prices Range
sections.html:
Closings in Greenbrier were busiest in September (21 sales across the two years) and slowest in January (5 sales). Sold prices ran from $145,000 to $700,000, a spread of 4.8x between the lowest and highest sale. 71% of homes closed at or above list price and 6% closed at least 5% below it.

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in Greenbrier
sections.html:
32% of the sales were detached homes and 68% were attached homes (townhomes or condos). The median home was about 1,256 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 1,026 to 1,576 square feet. 45% of the homes that sold had 2 bedrooms.

Most homes that sold were built between 1979 and 1989, with a median year built of 1984, so this is mostly homes from the 1970s through the 1990s.
